headline: Bruins get shellacked by Minnesota while Patriots prep for Germany
morning_brew: I am not gonna sugarcoat the absolute train wreck at the Garden last night. The Wild walked in and took us behind the woodshed, beating the Bruins by a four-goal margin and leaving me feeling like I just watched a horror movie. Watching our goalie struggle while the defense handed out open lanes like they were samples at a grocery store is not how I wanted to spend my Friday, especially since this makes it two straight losses. This team has been a tough watch over these last couple of nights, and if we don't start tightening up the gaps and finding some pride, the rest of the month is going to be a long climb that I am not looking forward to.

Switching gears to the gridiron, the Patriots have a massive kickoff ahead of them over in Germany against the Lions. It is a wicked weird feeling waking up to football before the coffee has even hit, but this squad needs a win to get things trending in the right direction. I am curious to see if the offensive line can finally hold up and whether Drake Maye can command the field against a gritty Detroit defense. My stomach is already in knots just thinking about the kickoff, and I really hope the boys bring their A-game across the pond because I don't think I can handle another morning of frustration.

Finally, the C's are back at the Garden later today for a matchup with Dallas. We have been on a roll lately, and it would be a hell of a statement to keep that momentum going against a tough Western Conference opponent. I plan on being planted in front of the television, hoping to see the defense lock down and the shots falling through the twine. It is a busy Sunday for all of us, and I am crossing my fingers that Boston finishes the day with a much better vibe than we started with, because Uncle Carmine is already grumpy enough about the state of the local hockey scene.

trend_watch.trend: David Pastrnak found the back of the net and added an assist during the home loss to Minnesota.
trend_watch.dans_take: Pasta is doing his part to drag this team along, but he can't carry the whole roster on his back every single night.

trend_watch.trend: Jeremy Swayman struggled between the pipes, stopping nineteen of the twenty-four shots he faced.
trend_watch.dans_take: That was a rough night at the office, but I have seen enough heart from him to know he can bounce back.

trend_watch.trend: Fraser Minten netted a power play goal to provide some life for the offense.
trend_watch.dans_take: It was nice to see him capitalize on the man advantage, even if the rest of the night was a total dud.

news_digest.headline: Wild beat Bruins behind two goals from Ryan Hartman
news_digest.dans_take: Watching the road winning streak extend at our expense was a bitter pill that I am still trying to wash down.

news_digest.headline: Week 10 betting preview: Analysis and predictions for Sunday
news_digest.dans_take: The experts can talk all they want, but the only thing that matters is whether we show up on that international field.
